verification.source_files_policy: strict: every file recorded in the schedule's source_files_sha256 (scripts/compare_town_movement.py included) must be present and byte-identical; a missing or changed file rejects the run

settings.json_format: compact separators, no indentation (reports are large)
settings.rotation_policy: Arm execution order within a frame is rotated by (trajectory_index + repeat + frame_index) % num_arms; session construction order within a repeat is rotated by (trajectory_index + repeat) % num_arms. Both realized orders are recorded per frame/repeat so no arm is systematically first or last.
settings.priming_policy: warm_buffered: once per (trajectory_kind, repeat) run, before any arm is constructed or timed, this script does one untimed ordinary buffered read of BOTH the whole and chunked container files for that method, discarding the bytes. macos_nocache: no priming is performed.
settings.session_policy: Every arm gets a freshly constructed session (stateless: none, by definition; lru{N}: an empty ChunkRegionCache; whole_resident: a new WholeMapResident) once per (method, mode, trajectory_kind, repeat), never reused across repeats. Each repeat records that session's own raw startup_metrics verbatim under repeats[].startup_metrics[arm], and first_viewport_ns = that startup total_ns + the repeat's frame 0 total_ns. If any arm's construction fails, the sessions already built for that repeat are closed before the error propagates.
settings.validation_policy: Every array returned by every arm, every frame, is checked (ndarray type, exact (height, width) shape, dtype, byte content against a crop of the in-memory original map) strictly after the timed call returns.
settings.timing_unit_policy: Raw values are integer nanoseconds and carry an _ns suffix: repeats[].frames[].arms[arm].total_ns, repeats[].startup_metrics[arm].total_ns and repeats[].trajectory_ns[arm]. Every aggregate is a stat block of median_ms/p95_ms/max_ms computed in milliseconds, so aggregate names are never given an _ns suffix.
settings.trajectory_total_policy: repeats[].trajectory_ns[arm] records, per repeat, that arm's raw startup_total_ns, frames_total_ns (sum of all frame total_ns) and total_ns_including_startup = startup + frames. The aggregates trajectory_total_including_startup and trajectory_total_movement_only are stats over those per-repeat totals. They are loader time only: not wall-clock frames, and they exclude rendering, physics, validation and report writing.
settings.memory_policy: --memory-repeats > 0 shells out once to scripts/measure_town_cache_memory.py with --schedule/--containers-dir/--cache-sizes/--repeats/--output, so memory is measured in fresh processes that never inherit this process's resident map. That script owns its own schema; it is folded in verbatim under report["memory"]["report"] with its path and sha256. Its existence is checked, and its output path refused if taken, before any container is written. Container hashes are re-verified AFTER it runs, so its reads are covered too.
settings.whole_resident_note: whole_resident has zero I/O/decode cost per .load() by construction in this benchmark (the map is already decoded and resident); this is not evidence that whole-map residency is universally the best choice -- it ignores memory cost and multi-map scenarios.

memory.note: --memory-repeats > 0 shells out once to scripts/measure_town_cache_memory.py with --schedule/--containers-dir/--cache-sizes/--repeats/--output, so memory is measured in fresh processes that never inherit this process's resident map. That script owns its own schema; it is folded in verbatim under report["memory"]["report"] with its path and sha256. Its existence is checked, and its output path refused if taken, before any container is written. Container hashes are re-verified AFTER it runs, so its reads are covered too.

report.scope: Independent memory sub-measurement: each (method, trajectory_kind, arm, repeat) is measured in its own fresh Python subprocess that imports horizon.town_cache / horizon.town_region fresh and is handed only a small request (arm name, two container paths, one trajectory's ROI list, one expected sha256) -- never the full map array and never the full schedule file. warm_buffered only. resident_decoded_bytes_* is the arm's own exact retained-array ledger (.resident_bytes); tracemalloc_*_bytes is traced Python/NumPy heap activity only, measured after imports+gc.collect(), split into startup (constructor) and movement (replay loop) phases with peak reset between them; process_rss_*_hwm_bytes is the absolute, monotonically non-decreasing OS RSS high-water mark for the whole process, not an attributable cache cost. None of this is a claim about physically cold SSD/controller reads; warm_buffered only describes this process priming the OS page cache once before each repeat. Only one output array is ever live per load step.
